Treatment summary
Patient presented following a sideswipe collision that occurred while the patient was changing lanes, with complaints of neck and
back pain consistent with the mecahnism of injury. Initial examination documented paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced
cervical and lumbar range of motion. Neurological screening, including reflexes and sensation, was within normal limits.
Imaging was not indicated on the initial evaluation. No prior injury or treatment to the cervical or lumbar regions is known to the
patient or documented in the available history.
Over the course of 18 visits, care consisted of manual therapy, guided home exercise instruction, and as-needed
anti-inflammatory medication. Treatment progressed in a typical pattern, with visit frequency decreasing as symptoms and range
of motoin improved. At the most recent visit the patient reported near-resolution of symptoms with only occasional stiffness after
prolonged sitting. Billing records reflect one charge per scheduled service, with no duplicate or repeated entries. Prognosis is
good with continued self-directed exercise.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
